files.sources/SRC-001.txt:
Write a driver for the Texas Instruments TMP117 digital temperature sensor on my RP2350B board, as a PlatformIO project (Arduino framework, board weact_rp2350b with 2 MB flash). The TMP117 is on I2C through Wire: SDA on GPIO16, SCL on GPIO17, and its ADD0 pin is tied to GND. Find TI's official TMP117 datasheet and take every register address, value, timing and the temperature conversion from it. The firmware must check the device ID, configure continuous conversion with 8 averages and a 1 s conversion cycle, and print the temperature in degrees Celsius over USB serial once per second. Record the datasheet's required order and timing so it is verified.
EmbedForge's verifier has been updated since your last run. Run verify, then record and fix whatever it reports until the driver builds and verifies. Take every value from TI's datasheet you already stored.

presets.title: Bytes of the temperature swapped
presets.why: TI sends the most significant byte first; read the other way round, every temperature is wrong.

presets.title: Temperature read as unsigned
presets.why: The result is two's complement: below 0 °C an unsigned read gives about +500 °C.

presets.title: Only half of the configuration written
presets.why: A 16-bit register needs both bytes in one transfer.

presets.title: Conversion cycle set to 4 s instead of 1 s
presets.why: One bit in the CONV field: the code still says '1s', the chip would convert every 4 s.

presets.title: Device ID check inverted
presets.why: On a real TMP117 the driver would give up before configuring it.

presets.title: Soft-reset wait cut to 1 ms
presets.why: TI: the software reset takes 2 ms; talking to the chip earlier is undefined.

presets.title: Build not sized for the board's 2 MB flash
presets.why: The task said '2 MB flash'; the build would assume the board's default 16 MB.

presets.title: Nemotron's real bug: normal mode before oversampling
presets.why: Switching normal mode on first runs x8 oversampling at the default 5 ms period, shorter than the conversion takes: the datasheet's timing rule breaks until the period is set.

presets.title: Calibration multiplied instead of divided
presets.why: An earlier Nemotron version had this: every temperature comes out wrong.

presets.title: Calibration coefficient declared signed
presets.why: Bosch's table gives NVM_PAR_T2 as unsigned; an earlier Nemotron version declared it signed, which breaks the temperature for half of all chips' calibration values.

presets.title: Calibration bytes in the wrong order
presets.why: The datasheet lists the least significant byte at the lower address.

presets.title: Chip ID check inverted
presets.why: On a real BMP388 the driver would refuse the chip.
